summary: Klaus-Josef Notz (1942–2013) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied theology at Philosophisch-Theologische Hochschule Benediktbeuern (1966–1971) and the University of Munich (1978–1984), where he later served as a Lehrbeauftragter in 1996.
Klemens Karlsson is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Uppsala University by 2000, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Schalk.

Knut A. Jacobsen (born 1956) works in religious studies and Indology. After earning his PhD at UC Santa Barbara (~1990–1994), he held professorships at the University of Bergen (from 1996) and the University of Oslo (~1996–1999).

Kobun Otogawa (1938–2002) studied Buddhism at Komazawa University, Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, Eihei-ji, and under Kodo Sawaki. He held posts at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center (1967–1970), Haiku Zendo (1970–1978), and Naropa University (2001).

Kodo Akino (1858–1934) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under teachers Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership posts at Komazawa University between 1892 and 1909.

Kodo Kawamura (1933–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his master's (~1956–1958) and doctorate (by 1984) at Komazawa University, where he also served as a professor from circa 1968 to 2004.
Kodo Nomura (1882–1963) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and later worked as a researcher at Taisho University.

Kodo Sawaki (1880–1965) studied at Senju-ji, Shinshu Takada-ha Senmon Gakko, and Horyuji Kangakuin, studying under several teachers. In Buddhist studies and philosophy, he served as a professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (~1949–1965).
Kodo Yamada (1866–1933) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who taught at both Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kodo Yotsuya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Komazawa University as a master's student under Shiro Matsumoto and obtained his PhD at the University of Hamburg.
Koen Wellens works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Charles Willemen at Ghent University and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under doctoral supervisor Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst (born 1959) is a scholar in Indology, sinology, and religious studies. He completed an MA at KU Leuven (~1982–1999) and studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1988–1992).

Kogen Mizuno (1901–2006) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo in 1928. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo and served as president of Komazawa University (1976).
Koichi Hiraoka (born 1961) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1980–1984) and is attested as a visiting professor at Shuchiin University in 2026.

Koichi Hokazono works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University, later holding posts at Kagoshima International University (attested 1991–2000) and Kyushu University (attested 1995).

Koichi Shinohara (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He served as professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and as senior lecturer in religious studies at Yale University (~2004–2017).

Koichi Takahashi (born 1973) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima and Akira Saito, subsequently serving there as assistant (2005) and professor (2026).

Koichi Yokoyama (1940–2023) studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and under Gyōin Hashimoto. He served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University from circa 1974 to 2006.
Koin Takada (1924–1998) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Ryukoku University (~1941–1944). He was a disciple of Gyōin Hashimoto (~1937–1978), whom he succeeded in 1967.

Koji Kamioka (1938–2024) studied Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara (~1957–1963). He taught as a lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969) and was a staff member at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).
